Cross-tenant isolation is proven by tests that try and fail. Named tests attempt to read and to write another venue's sponsors, codes, redemptions, rollups and reports, and to read a couple workspace from a venue session, each asserting refusal at the data layer rather than only at the route. Evidence: app/src/server/cross-tenant-isolation.test.mjs and tenant-scope.test.mjs extended with the sponsored-venue cases, named and passing. (E08.04, E08.05)

Every venue-facing and couple-facing route is enumerated in a committed manifest with its required role, and a test fails when a route exists without an entry. Anonymous, wrong-venue, wrong-role and revoked-member requests are each asserted refused. Evidence: app/scripts/check-route-manifest.mjs extended plus the authorisation-matrix test output. (E08.05, E07.18)

Invitation tokens survive five named attacks, one test each: guessing with entropy stated in bits and redemption rate-limited per address and per account with the enumeration arithmetic shown, reuse after redemption, forwarding to a different account, replay of a captured redemption request, and two concurrent redemptions of the same code. Evidence: five named tests, all passing. (E08.06)

A restore actually happened. pnpm recovery:drill is run against a real backup of every production database carrying venue or couple data; the restored copy is queried to confirm a known sponsored workspace and its redemptions are present; and wall-clock time from decision to restored is recorded. RPO and RTO are recorded as measured numbers, not targets. Evidence: the drill output with timestamps and the restored-row proof. A backup that has never been restored is not a backup. (E08.09)

The incident runbook names a person, a channel and a clock for each of: breach affecting couple data, breach affecting venue data, total outage, silent data corruption, and a wrongly issued or wrongly expired entitlement. It records the 72-hour GDPR Article 33 notification clock and where the DPC is contacted. It has been walked through once as a tabletop, and the absence of paid on-call is recorded as an accepted limitation of the zero budget. Evidence: the runbook and the tabletop record. (E08.08, E08.12, D-015 Q5)

Billing is tested with real money once, before any venue is invoiced. One founding agreement at EUR 1,000 is charged and refunded in production; the immutable founding-rate flag and historical price record are written and cannot be edited from the operator UI; the invoice states the price as inclusive of VAT at the prevailing rate; and the payment is individually identifiable so treatment can be corrected retrospectively. Evidence: the transaction ID, the refund ID, the invoice PDF showing the VAT wording, and the immutability test. (E08.01, E08.02, E15.02, D-021, R-018)

Renewal, failed payment, grace and lapse each fire against a clock in test: renewal invoice, reminder, failed-payment retry schedule, grace-period end, and lapse, with the D-020 survival rule asserted, that a lapsed venue's already-redeemed workspaces keep full term plus Keepsake and only new issuance stops. Evidence: a time-travel test covering all five transitions plus the survival assertion. (E08.03, D-020 point 2)

Upload handling is honest about what a zero budget buys: file type validated by content rather than extension, size limits enforced server-side, private storage with signed time-limited URLs, no user-supplied file served from an origin that can execute it, and EXIF stripped from milestone photographs. The absence of commercial malware scanning is recorded as an accepted residual with the founder's note. Evidence: the tests, the storage configuration, and the recorded residual. (E08.07)

Performance budgets are measured on the surfaces that carry the product's claim: the shared Timeline on a mid-range mobile over a throttled connection, the portal Overview, and the couple briefing. pnpm budgets:check and pnpm performance:measure produce recorded numbers against stated budgets and a regression fails the build. Evidence: the budget file, the measured run, the CI wiring. (E08.10)

Instrumentation reconciles across three layers at least once. A scripted run creates an invitation, redeems it, performs a first meaningful action, publishes a Timeline and enters Keepsake; each of those five transitions is asserted present in the event stream, in the daily rollup and in the venue's report, with counts matching at every layer, duplicate source events proven idempotent, and every number in the report carrying its metric dictionary version, denominator, reporting window and coverage state. Evidence: the script and its three-layer output. (E09.01, E09.02, E09.03, E09.09, E07.15)

The demonstration fixture is deterministic and its imagery's provenance is recorded. The one-action demo reset restores the canonical Glenmara House and Mara-and-Finn state identically across all four products and the portal on two consecutive runs; every demonstration image records how it was generated (model, prompt or source, date), because D-012 replaced licensing with generation and there is no licence to file; and a named reviewer confirms no unapproved real venue or couple material appears. Evidence: the reset diffed twice, the image provenance register, the reviewer verdict. (E09.06, E09.07, E09.08, E09.12, D-012, A-007, R-011)

Release engineering is executed, not documented. The three steps in studio/content/hq/operator-todos/open-signal-studio-2026-09-01.md are individually completed and ticked: the redeploy that flips the statically generated surfaces, the marketing-CTA decision, and the /app allowlist decision. Every venue-reachable URL is re-fetched after the deploy and confirmed to show post-launch state, and the rollback procedure has been executed once against a staging deploy. Evidence: the closed operator-todo, the post-deploy fetch of each URL, and the rollback run output. (E08.12, D-007, DEP-005)
